title: Generics
objectives: Use generic types and methods for type safety
Understand type erasure and its limits

sections.markdown: Generics let you write classes and methods parameterized over types, giving compile-time type safety and removing casts.
**PECS** — Producer Extends, Consumer Super. Use `? extends T` when you only read from a structure, `? super T` when you only write to it.
Generics use **type erasure**: type parameters exist at compile time and are erased at runtime. So you can't do `new T()` or `instanceof List<String>`.
Using raw types (`List` instead of `List<String>`) — it disables generic checks and invites ClassCastException at runtime. Always parameterize.

flashcards.back: Producer Extends, Consumer Super: read with ? extends T, write with ? super T.
Generic type info is removed at runtime; the JVM sees raw types, so no new T() or generic instanceof.
They bypass compile-time checks and reintroduce ClassCastException risk.

quiz.explain: An upper-bounded wildcard is a producer — you read, you can't safely add.

quiz.q: Generics in Java are implemented via…
quiz.explain: Type parameters are erased at runtime (unlike C# reified generics).
Erasure means the runtime doesn't know T's actual type.

challenges.text: Write a generic max(List<T extends Comparable<T>>) method.
Implement a generic Stack<T> with push/pop/peek.
Write a copy method using PECS bounded wildcards correctly.
Build a type-safe heterogeneous container using Class<T> as keys.
